problem: "avoids the heat of a linear regulator" reads as if PWM itself removes the heat. PWM only cuts loss because the switching transistor is either fully on (low V, low loss) or fully off; the sentence can mislead a student into thinking duty cycle alone sets the heat.
fix: "Its fixed period suits switching circuits, and a switching transistor that is fully on or fully off wastes far less heat than a linear regulator passing the same current."

problem: "Some syllabi call this pulse-width modulation" comes right after the duty-cycle definition, so "this" seems to point at D, not at PWM (which the chapter is already about). The sentence confuses more than it helps.
fix: "Some syllabi call D the duty ratio."

problem: The answer says the switching period must be much shorter than the motor's mechanical time constant, but the current ripple is set by the electrical time constant L/R. Only the speed ripple is set by the mechanical time constant. A student may conclude inductance smoothing depends on the mechanical constant.
fix: "The switching period must be much shorter than the motor's electrical time constant L/R so the current stays smooth, and much shorter than the mechanical time constant so the speed stays smooth."

problem: "drives heaters through a relay or SSR" does not say that a mechanical relay cannot switch at normal PWM frequencies. A student may try 1 kHz PWM on a relay coil and get chatter and burnt contacts.
fix: "drives heaters through an SSR, or through a relay only with a slow PWM period of a second or more so the contacts do not chatter."
